pulls.title: 8392008: Fix CDS race when mapping into reserved regions on Windows
pulls.author: roberttoyonaga
pulls.body_excerpt: ### Summary: The goal of this PR is to eliminate the following race-prone pattern in CDS archive mapping code on Windows: - Reserve a large range. - Release the entire range. - Quickly map archive file sections into subregions within the original range. The reason this pattern exists is because Windows previously did not allow mapping into reserved regions. It also did not allow splitting up a reserved region. pulls.author: TobiHartmann
pulls.body_excerpt: In `TestPrimitiveUnboxing::testDeadLoop`, the division by zero in the nested loop makes the second loop unreachable. When the entry of the second loop dies, the I/O Phi collapses to the I/O projection of the unboxing `intValue` call, creating a self referencing call: ``` [I/O PhiNode] -> [intValue()] -> [I/O ProjNode] ^ | └──────────────────────────────────┘ ``` Because the return value is unused, macro expansion eliminates the `intValue()` and attempts to bypass its I/O projection: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/a944ec3aff9550fd498c37559a21510b8dd6ca39/src/hotspot/share/opto/macro.cpp#L1
